text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `PD#54321` — high DB connection queueing / redis client saturation detected for prod-us-east-1
Alex: got the page, I'm oncall. seeing 503 spikes from api-gateway + SLO alerts in console.
Maria: looking at grafana now — Postgres active connections at ~950/1000, pgbouncer pool queued 420, redis connected_clients at 12k (normally ~3k).
Alex: @Maria can you confirm which service is creating the spike? any recent deploys?
Maria: no deploys in last 2h (deploy-bot shows nothing), traffic ramp looks correlated with batch-worker-v2 job started at 12:03 UTC.
Ryan: that batch kicks off a large number of short-lived DB transactions and uses a Redis pub/sub fanout. Could be the culprit.
Kate: I'm on DB. running `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active';` returns 948. also seeing many `idle in transaction` from worker batch job.
Alex: mitigation plan: 1) pause/disable batch job, 2) increase pgbouncer max_client_connections, 3) scale up redis node capacity (or add replica), 4) contact support for customer-facing comms.
Maria: agreed — I'll kill the batch job controller and scale pgbouncer pool. Doing `kubectl scale deployment batch-worker-v2 --replicas=0 -n prod-jobs` now.
Ryan: pause API clients that fanout to redis? we can set maintenance header to reject non-essential traffic.
Alex: @Ryan go ahead — add 503 for /internal/fanout endpoints for 5m.
Ryan: applied rate-limiting rule in the gateway: `rate-limit: 10rpm` for fanout routes.
Maria: pgbouncer max_client_connections bumped from 2000 -> 4000 on pool config and reloaded: `pgbouncer -R` done.
Kate: applying a quick connection cutoff on worker role: `ALTER ROLE batch_worker CONNECTION LIMIT 5;` to stop new workers from opening many connections.
Alex: Redis scaling — @Kate can you trigger scaling of the redis-cluster prod-us-east-1 from 3x.medium -> 3x.large?
Kate: requested horizontal resize through infra autoscaler; also enabling AOF to reduce connection churn temporarily.
deploy-bot: No recent deploys detected in last 2 hours.
Maria: seeing pgbouncer queue length drop in charts from 420 -> 30 after batch stopped. Postgres active now 320.
Alex: any errors left in application logs?
Ryan: saw a handful of `timeout waiting for connection` errors at 12:07, now tail shows normal request flow returning 200s.
Josh: support note: customers A, B, C reported elevated 5xx rates starting 12:05 UTC. I've opened a private incident update thread to CS leads.
Olivia: product note: at-risk customers flagged (high-traffic accounts) — recommend we send an initial email with apology and ETA.
Alex: acking the PD alert to stop page noise.
incident-bot: PagerDuty `PD#54321` acknowledged by Alex at 1766667940.
Maria: Redis connected clients down to ~3.5k, used memory still high but not critical.
Kate: Postgres queue stable, active connections steady ~310, connection queue < 10.
Alex: good containment. Next: follow-up items — 1) add batch job concurrency limit in code + fix idle-in-transaction issue, 2) hardening pgbouncer configs, 3) review redis client pooling in the worker.
Ryan: I'll open Github issue to add exponential backoff and connection pooling for the batch worker — assigning to @team-backend.
Maria: will draft a short runbook entry for this pattern (batch fanout -> db+redis saturation) with playbook steps and escalation thresholds.
Josh: drafting customer comms — will share SMS/email templates in the CS thread.
Olivia: can we estimate outage window? looks like elevated errors from 12:05 -> 12:18 UTC, about 13 minutes.
Alex: marking incident as "mitigated" at 12:18 UTC in incident tracker. root cause provisional: runaway batch-worker concurrency causing pooled resource exhaustion (pg + redis).
Maria: adding note: observed many `idle in transaction` entries — immediate bugfix required to commit/rollback promptly.
Kate: I'll run a short health-check script and leave a cron to alert earlier if pgbouncer queue > 50 for > 2m. adding alert -> `pgbouncer_queue > 50 for 2m` -> page oncall.
Alex: any outstanding tasks before handoff?
Maria: I'll stay on for 10 more minutes to confirm stability, then hand to next oncall.
Alex: ok handoff timeline: Alex oncall until 12:30 UTC, then @Ryan covers.
incident-bot: PagerDuty `PD#54321` resolved by Alex at 1766668110.
Ryan: acknowledged handoff. will monitor dashboards and follow up on the github ticket.
Olivia: follow-up action for product: review SLA breach window and prepare a billing credit evaluation if needed.
Josh: CS will prepare proactive outreach to impacted customers with incident summary + mitigation steps.
Maria: postmortem owner volunteers? I'm happy to draft initial timeline and RCA.
Ryan: I'll co-author and add remediation PRs for the batch worker.
Alex: thanks everyone. quick retro note: we need automatic throttles on batch jobs if downstream queues exceed thresholds.
Kate: adding to infra backlog: autoscale pgbouncer pool automatically when queue > 100 and scale down after 10m stable.
Maria: leaving final check: all graphs stable for 5m, no new pager events.
Alex: handoff complete at 12:25 UTC. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
